title: Ops coyote standup — week of 2028-03-21
content:
TL;DR: This week we had a transient NVMe-related tail-latency incident that impacted the embeddings pipeline for ~45 minutes (S3 backed cached keys + local NVMe IOPS contention). No customer data loss; a handful of high-latency requests triggered automated failover. Error budget consumption for embeddings 99p rose to 16% this week — we need an action to keep it below 10% next quarter.

Quick meeting notes (standup cadence — Tue/Wed/Thu):
- Tue 09:30: quick sync: triage current alerts, check SLO dashboards
- Wed 11:00: incident debrief (this doc summarizes)
- Thu 15:00: follow-up & plan-of-record review

Incidents (concise):
1) Incident: embeddings-tail-2028-03-18 — Severity: Sev2
   - Window: 2028-03-18 13:17 -> 2028-03-18 14:05 UTC
   - Symptom: sudden spike in 99th pct latency for embeddings.generate (from ~180ms to >3s).
   - Mitigation applied: routed new requests to warm fallback cluster, increased async prefetch buffer, manual scale-up of embedding-workers in us-west-2.
   - Root cause (initial RCA): nvme device on a host entered degraded mode under write pressure from a background checkpoint job (ML cache eviction). This caused IO queuing and slowed local kv-cache reads.
   - Long-form notes: background job evictions coincide with heavy prefix cache writes from a specific new customer workload (high embedding churn). The autoscaler didn't trigger fast enough because requests were CPU-light but IO-heavy; current autoscaler uses CPU + queue length heuristics but not NVMe latency.
   - Customer impact: increased tail latency for a subset of developers' tests and nightly batch tasks; production apps fell back to cached model variant (slightly higher error budget use). No failed requests persisted, retries handled most attempts.
   - Post-incident action items (owners):
       * Add NVMe latency metric to autoscaler triggers (Arjun) — due 2028-03-28
       * Add eviction/job throttle during peak traffic windows (Sofia) — RFC by 2028-03-24
       * Replace degraded NVMe node and mark host pool health (Noah) — done 2028-03-18
       * Follow-up: formal RCA doc & timeline (Maya) — draft by 2028-03-22 (linked SRE-4827)

2) Incident: small memory leak in routing-proxy-2028-03-15 — Severity: Sev3
   - Observed memory growth on proxy pods, periodic restarts triggered ephemeral increase in 5xxs.
   - Mitigation: rolling restart and bump of probe thresholds; engineering to ship patch next week (Evelyn).

SLOs & error budgets:
- Embeddings.generate: SLO (p99 < 1s) — current rolling 30d: 98.64% (error budget remaining: 22%); last 7d: 83.9% (error budget burn: 16% this week).
- Text.generate: SLOs stable; 99p at 0.45s.
- Recommendations: do a targeted canary for the nvme-aware autoscaler change behind feature flag, monitor p99 for 48 hours before rollout.

On-call handoff notes (next rotation):
- Current on-call: week of Mar 13–19 — Arjun (primary), Sofia (secondary).
- Next on-call: Mar 20–26 — Noah (primary), Evelyn (secondary).
- Handoff checklist (to leave in thread):
   * Outstanding alerts: watch embeddings p99, routing-proxy memory alerts, autoscaler queue-length SLO alert
   * Keys/credentials: KMS rotation scheduled 2028-04-02 (no action now)
   * Scheduled maintenance: db compaction window Fri 2028-03-24 02:00–04:00 UTC (expect brief latency spikes)

Runbooks & known gaps:
- Runbook: embeddings-kv-cache-degradation — exists but lacks NVMe-specific mitigation steps. Marked as "needs update".
- Gap: no durable metric for NVMe stall rate in our exporter stack; currently estimated via node disk_utilization and iostat snapshots.
- Proposal: add iowait-based alert and per-pod nvme_latency histogram (Evelyn + infra) — triage/PR by 2028-03-27.

Operational experiments / trials:
- Autoscaler experiment: add NVMe latency and async queue depth as extra features for decisioning. Small canary to 10% of embedding requests starting 2028-03-25. Measure p99 and tail-burn. Owner: Arjun.
- Cache eviction policy trial: soft-throttle background checkpoints during heavy traffic windows. Owner: Sofia.

Action item tracker (short):
- ARJ-01: Add NVMe latency metric to autoscaler & expose to HPA framework (Arjun) — 2028-03-28
- SOP-05: Update embeddings runbook with NVMe troubleshooting steps (Evelyn) — 2028-03-27
- SVC-112: Postmortem write-up and timeline (Maya) — 2028-03-22
- OPS-78: Autoscaler canary rollout plan & monitoring dashboards (Noah) — 2028-03-24
- ENG-200: Patch routing-proxy memory leak (Evelyn) — target release 2028-03-30

Decisions made this week:
- Prioritize NVMe-aware autoscaling work over expansion of shard count (we can scale vertically faster than changing sharding logic).
- Short-term customer impact mitigation: widen fallback model pool by 1 variant for high-churn customers for the next 2 weeks. (Emergency guardrails in place)

Open questions / blockers:
- Is there a cost-acceptable telemetry approach for per-pod NVMe histograms? We need a low-cardinality, high-signal metric — team input requested.
- Can product partner flag heavy-churn customers so we can schedule quieter eviction windows? (Sophie from product has been pinged)

Notes to self / informal:
- Observability surfaces got cleaner after the rollout of per-route dashboards, but host-level IO blind spots are biting. — worth a quick session with observability team to align exporters.
- Consider a short "IO storm" tabletop runbook exercise in April.

Appendix / quick links:
- Related tickets: SRE-4827, SRE-4899, SRE-4952
- Debug snapshot: s3://redwood-debug/2028-03-18/embeddings-io-trace.tgz
- Pager history: https://pager.redwood.internal/archives/2028-03-18-embeddings

If anything should be moved to "urgent" for the next on-call handover, flag here in the doc. Otherwise we'll plan the NVMe autoscaler canary for next week and follow up in Thu 15:00 sync.

— Maya
